description:
ROUND-38 EMISSION ITEM (filed s500p; perf round 37 was RUNTIME-ONLY).

FINDING: passing an ARRAY to a sub (`f(@a)`) promotes every RAW slot of @a to a box IN PLACE (%p-flatten-run -> %p-elem-cell), because @_ aliases the caller's elements -- and an array slice in a `map` block (`map { @deck[$_, $_ + $m] } …`) builds alias boxes (%p-alias-aelem) that the map immediately copies away (%p-map-copy-scalar).  When the callee is a SIGNATURE sub whose parameters COPY (`sub f (@deck)`), or the slice sits in a copying position, no alias is ever observable, so the promotion is pure cost -- and it recurs every call, because the caller's array is re-assigned from the (raw) map result each iteration.

PROFILE LINE (s500p Step 0, main 209e7533): 1009-Perfect-shuffle (0.65 s vs perl 0.22 s): %p-flatten-run 28.9 % total (make-p-box 17.8 % of it), p-aslice 25.9 % total, %make-p-box 15.1 % self, p-aref-argbox 10.9 %, p-map 50.9 % total.
  Program: `sub perfect_shuffle (@deck) { my $middle = @deck / 2; map { @deck[$_, $_ + $middle] } 0..$middle-1 }` called as `@shuffled = perfect_shuffle @shuffled` in a loop.

WHY NOT RUNTIME: the runtime cannot know the callee copies or that the slice's consumer copies; the compiler does (the signature is visible at the call site's sub; the map block's result position is a copy position).  A Kind-A licence ("args-copy": the callee binds @_ only through a signature / `my (...) = @_` and never touches @_ otherwise) would let the call pass the raw storage; a slice in a map-block return could use a non-aliasing read.  Size first by hand-editing the emitted .lisp (ab-lisp method).


=== DONE (s501q) ===
(i) SHIPPED as Kind-A `args-copy`: a body whose only reading of @_ is a leading `my (LIST) = @_;` (and a signature's arity check) is emitted `(p-args-body :copy â¦)`, which builds @_ from VALUES (%p-flatten-arg-values) -- the caller's raw element slots are never promoted.  The licence is a CALLEE fact (the body cannot observe @_), so `&f(@a)`, `&$r(@a)`, methods and a later redefinition need no call-site proof; the p-raw-params path builds its argument list from values the same way.  (ii) SHIPPED runtime-only: p-map's compiler macro rewrites a block whose VALUE is an rvalue slice to the copying read %p-aslice-copy / %p-hslice-copy (#1205's consumer rule with p-map as consumer; perl copies map results -- `$_++ for map { @a[0,1] } 1` leaves @a alone, probed 5.40.3).  ir-spec Â§5.2 + Â§3.2d.
